Essay:
The topic I have chosen focuses on the negative thoughts associated with struggling to make friends at university. Since starting university, I have struggled to make new friends. Even when I do, the connections often feel shallow, just quick greetings and nothing more. I cannot help but wonder if the issue lies with me, perhaps it’s my personality or the fact that I am introverted that pushes people away. I believe it is a social reality that people who do not have many friends are often labeled as 'weird.' That perception is what fuels these thoughts, and they tend to worsen at the start of each new semester when I have to enter new classes.

I asked ChatGPT to suggest the most suitable approach based on how I was feeling. It identified Compassion Focused Therapy (CFT) as a fitting method, given that my main struggle was with self-criticism. I then requested a single prompt that could guide me through the process of reframing and improving how I feel about myself.

ChatGPT prompt for CFT:



I chose to use ChatGPT for this conversation because I'm more familiar with it and feel that it connects with me better, as I use this platform daily.

ChatGPT guided me step by step using the principles of CFT, offering meaningful insights. It helped me realize that even if I had many friends at university, I might still struggle with thoughts like, “Do my friends even like me?” This understanding made me feel more at ease with myself, as I no longer felt the need to put on a “fake” version of me just to be liked by others.

Additionally, it encouraged me to recognize the positive side of my self-criticism, that it stems from a desire to protect myself from being hurt when my efforts go unnoticed or unappreciated. Through this, I learned something deeper about myself: I genuinely value meaningful connections and wish to build strong, lasting friendships rather than superficial ones. I have also realised that I should not be disappointed in myself for caring deeply about the relationships I form.
 
After completing this assignment, I feel a genuine sense of relief and self-acceptance. I have learned to shift my perspective from labeling myself as “weird” to understanding that perhaps others simply have not seen the good in me yet and that is completely fine. In university, many connections can be quite surface-level, so not having a large circle of friends does not define my worth or how “normal” I am compared to others. What matters more is the authenticity of the relationships I do form.
This reflection made me realise that constantly comparing myself to others only deepens feelings of inadequacy. Instead, I can learn to appreciate who I am and focus on forming genuine connections with people who truly value me. I also gained a new perspective which is that building friendships should not be a one-sided effort. Meaningful relationships require mutual care and commitment from both sides. Being comfortable with myself is far more meaningful than trying to fit into the social reality.

Question: In our daily lives, we engage in countless conversations with others and with ourselves. Some resemble the transmission or interaction models of communication, while others are transformative—aligned with the transactional model—leading to new perspectives and the co-creation of meaning. Could such an “Ah-Ha” moment also emerge from a conversation with AI? We are living in a rapid prototyping era in which AI has accelerated the development of functional prototypes that allow us to explore the synergy between artificial intelligence and humanity. In this assignment, you will design and use conversational AI to guide a process of self-discovery and reflect critically on the experience.
Essay:
For this assignment, I chose to explore the theme of family. While I have often described family as the most important thing in life, I realised that I had never paused to articulate how deeply they shape the person I am now. I wanted to understand why family feels central to my life and whether that awareness could be expressed in a clearer manner.
Using ChatGPT, as my reflective partner, I discovered that family is not simply an influence among many, but the one constant that has been present from the beginning and will always be there till the end, acting as a lifelong anchor to my life.
I chose ChatGPT as my conversational agent as I found it the most flexible and has the
highest ability to sustain dialogue compared to its counterparts like Perplexity, Gemini etc. I designed it to act as my reflective coach, giving it specific instructions through prompt
engineering
•	“Ask one thought-provoking question at a time about my family.”
•	“Encourage me to connect personal experiences to values and life decisions.”
•	“Maintain a supportive yet challenging tone to help me uncover new insights.”
I refined these prompts iteratively. Initially, the AI’s questions were general, but through multiple iterations, I calibrated them to probe deeper into family dynamics like
relationships with siblings, parental guidance, intergenerational lessons like ethics and culture. This iterative process reflects rapid prototyping, where small adjustments to the AI’s instructions led to meaningful differences in the conversation’s depth and clarity. The dialogue demonstrated transactional model of communication, where meaning emerged through the interplay of my reflections and the AI’s questions, rather than through a simple one-way exchange. I also recognised the potential of multi-agent LLMs, where one agent could simulate a family member’s perspective and another a future self, creating richer, multi-dimensional reflection.
The conversation prompted me to recall formative memories: as an ex-national athlete, they would often come to my matches and regardless of the score, I would be embraced with either happiness or encouragement, never anything negative. Small disagreements with my siblings taught me patience and de-escalation, and family routines that fostered a sense of stability and belonging. Initially I considered these lessons individually. But with AI’s probing, it led me to see how all these memories are all interconnected, with family being the scaffolding for the values imbedded in me today: resilience, humility, empathy, support and respect. A particularly impactful realisation came when AI asked me how family influenced my choices beyond emotional support. From having the strong mental strength to go through tough matches or academic challenges, to navigating life decisions like finding a life partner and good friends, I realised that all of these were rooted in the
knowledge that my family would always be there for me, offering both guidance and
 
reassurance. Previously I attributed these traits and decisions to my personal drive, but now I understand that they are intertwined with the constant presence of my family.
Another “Ah-Ha” moment emerged when I reflected on how family differs from other relationships. Friends, colleagues, mentors, classmates will come and go, but family will always be there. You can have many friends or be popular, but ultimately you only have 1
family in your whole life. They are not merely supportive; they actively shape my worldview and interpersonal approach. For example, the way I choose friends or life partners mirrors lessons internalised from my family dynamics. Values like reliability, loyalty, support, trust are the main things I look for when making friends, I would rather have only 1 friend that I can count on than multiple ‘fake’ friends who might not be there for me in times of need or leave when things get tough; a direct representation of having only 1 family is more than enough.
The AI-guided reflection process was new to me, but it highlighted both its potential and limitations. Its neutrality provided a safe space to confide in without any fear of judgement.
Through the iterative prompts, it enabled me to also uncover connections I had not
consciously recognised. However, AI is unable to perceive emotional nuance or respond empathetically to subtle cues, a limitation that human counsellors would overcome naturally. Regardless, the experience was transformative. I now view family not as important, but as the foundation and enduring influence shaping my identity, decisions and my future. Recognising that family is present “from the beginning and will always be there till the end” deepens my appreciation and motivate me to maintain these bonds intentionally and carry it forward into my future family (if permitted). This exercise also
demonstrated the broader potential of AI as a partner in co-creating meaning and
facilitating self-discovery. This highlighted how thoughtful design and prompt iteration and guide reflection with exceptional depth.

Some resemble the transmission or interaction models of communication, while others are transformative—aligned with the transactional model—leading to new perspectives and the co-creation of meaning. Could such an “Ah-Ha” moment also emerge from a conversation with AI? We are living in a rapid prototyping era in which AI has accelerated the development of functional prototypes that allow us to explore the synergy between artificial intelligence and humanity. In this assignment, you will design and use conversational AI to guide a process of self-discovery and reflect critically on the experience.
Essay:
Home Away From Home - AIH Information to Transformation


I discovered the true meaning of loneliness in a bathroom stall. Sick, dizzy, and shaking in Singapore, I had no family to call and no one waiting for me at home. Although the committee at the event helped me get medicine and a ride back to my dorm, the aching head and blurry vision made the reality sink in: I would be returning to an empty place — at least a place with no one who cared — for the next seven years. This experience inspired this self-discovery project, in which I explored how my social reality (my experience of loneliness and homesickness) was shaped by moving abroad and how a conversational AI could help me reframe these intense emotions.
I chose ChatGPT as my platform because it is free, accessible, and the tool I am most familiar with. Its simplicity made it a practical choice for experimenting with a conversational agent in the context of self-discovery. My first step was to essentially ‘program’ the AI, asking it to adopt the role of a supportive CBT (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy) coach. Using AI for AI, it helped me create the given prompt:
You are a supportive CBT coach: calm, empathetic, and non-judgmental. Your role is to guide me step by step through grounding, identifying thoughts and feelings, spotting distortions, reframing into balanced perspectives, and suggesting coping strategies. Responses should be short, clear, and gentle, encouraging reflection without overwhelming. If distress is high, the agent should begin with grounding before moving to reframing.
Then so it began. The AI followed a chain-of-thought approach, guiding me step by step from grounding exercises to deeper reflection rather than jumping straight to solutions. Starting off with breathing exercises and after, asked me questions regarding the issue at hand. I talked about feeling sick, alone, and terrified in a foreign country. The chatbot’s initial response was stiff telling me “Being sick alone feels scary, there are people and resources I can reach out to,” to me, it fell flat. It felt like a textbook solution than genuine empathy, and I knew I needed to push deeper.
Even after pushing deeper though, it listed off too-practical solutions like keeping a first-aid kit and saving emergency contacts. While helpful, it frustrated me because I wasn’t looking for a to-do list. So, I reframed it one more time. I elaborated on the “what-ifs”, the dread of not always being lucky. I emphasized on my fears this time, of the conscious choice to live abroad. This, I believe, is where the conversation started to genuinely get deeper. In a way, the AI was performing a simple form of sentiment analysis, recognizing my sadness and fear, and responding with what could be seen as affective computing, offering empathetic guidance.
The Aha-Moment finally arrived as it said: “Feeling lonely doesn’t mean you made the wrong choice.” I think that was really eye opening for me. From there, the
 
conversation became a true exploration. The AI prompted me to notice the small ways I had grown since moving, the said “Growth doesn’t erase fear, but it coexists with it. You can be scared and still capable.” In this process, the AI seemed to interpret my emotions more than just categorical, in fact rather dimensional.
We ended with a discussion of daily routines that could help me feel less alone, looping back to giving more practical advice which I didn’t really mind anymore. It advised me to do easy steps like hanging pictures of my family/friends (Fig. 1), eating foods that would bring comfort, and checking in through a text or message. Closing the conversation with the same breathing exercises we had started with, I felt a sense of peace that had been missing. It was a strange journey, but I left feeling genuinely heard, motivated, and even putting its advice into practice.















Hung pictures of my family and friends (Fig. 1)

In the beginning, I didn’t expect much from a ChatBot. I was frustrated from time to time that it gave me such practical and surface level solution. But as the conversation went on and I poured more into detail and gave emphasis on the feeling aspect, it began to console me. And, as embarrassing as it may sound, I was brought to tears throughout the conversation. I know it’s only been a short month but I really do miss everything and as time goes on, I question whether being here is the right choice.
One sentence that stuck with me was: “Feeling lonely doesn’t mean you made the wrong choice.” While a human might have reached that conclusion faster, this interaction showed me the value of structured reflection. The AI’s guidance, though sometimes rigid, helped me notice and name my emotions, and to see that fear and growth can coexist. But I realized that sometimes I don’t need solutions, but acknowledgment, which I feel a human is more capable of. But this did help. Moving forward, I can approach moments of homesickness with more self-compassion and deliberate small steps to care for myself.

Question: In our daily lives, we engage in countless conversations with others and with ourselves. Some resemble the transmission or interaction models of communication, while others are transformative—aligned with the transactional model—leading to new perspectives and the co-creation of meaning. Could such an “Ah-Ha” moment also emerge from a conversation with AI? We are living in a rapid prototyping era in which AI has accelerated the development of functional prototypes that allow us to explore the synergy between artificial intelligence and humanity. In this assignment, you will design and use conversational AI to guide a process of self-discovery and reflect critically on the experience.
Essay:
Information to Transformation
The fear of failure has always been stuck in me throughout my educational journey. This assignment was an opportunity for me to explore whether I could gain greater awareness in this area using ChatGPT. I was staring at the chat screen unsure of how I could start a conversation that can help me to share my thoughts and receive an answer I’m looking for. Then it came to my mind, why not openly share my thoughts with ChatGPT and let it guide me on how I can prompt effectively.
To begin, I used a role-based prompt by asking ChatGPT to think in the view of a Ph.D. psychologist with years of professional experience and an expert prompt engineer. I wanted ChatGPT to provide prompts that could guide me through a process of psychotherapy focused on reframing my thoughts as I go through this tough time. My input also included meta-prompting as I got an AI (ChatGPT) to generate prompts for an LLM.
Interestingly, even though I only asked for some prompts, ChatGPT provided me with a three-step framework on how I could structure the session. It provided a grounding prompt that I can copy and paste into the LLM. The grounding prompt helps our conversation stay relevant to my topic. Rather than seeking generic responses, I wanted ChatGPT to analyse and breakdown my thought process step-by-step. Hence, I applied the chain of thought prompting method by beginning with the grounding prompt provided. I also added a sentence of “Please guide me through step-by-step as it is my first time experiencing this.”
Curious on how ChatGPT would respond to my multiple requests, I proceeded with the conversation. ChatGPT began by getting me to take three slow breathes and checked if I was ready to explore what’s troubling me. I provided rich context in my responses, describing how and why I was feeling certain emotions. For example, when ChatGPT asked what had been weighing me down lately. I gave the context of me feeling anxious due to overwhelming expectations in life. My fear of failure was getting worse and I often felt like I'm the only one that is failing behind.
What surprised me was how ChatGPT did not rush to provide me with multiple solutions. Instead, it acknowledges my efforts and emotions. ChatGPT also said that we could take small steps together to unpack beneath my thoughts. It also highlighted key points in my responses such as my emotion and sense of falling behind. It proceeded to ask me my feelings when I said I’m the only one failing and lacking behind. Throughout the conversation, ChatGPT was patient and check in with my emotions after each question. When my response becomes emotionally negative, ChatGPT guided me through slow breathing exercises. This method helped calm my emotions before continuing. The whole process gave me a sense of assurance and validation which allowed me to open up more deeply. What’s more, ChatGPT also guided me to find alternative perspectives rather than staying trapped in my negative thought.
 
Through this exercise, I became more aware of how my fear of failure was rooted in self-criticism. I realized that I often put an end to myself when I just begin this journey like a newborn. I recognized the effort I was already putting in even though I might not yet see the results I hoped for. I am still progressing and learning at my own pace. I also discovered that asking question is a strength, not a weakness because it shows my willingness to learn and grow. The most encouraging thing ChatGPT did was creating a mantra for me, which I printed and placed on my desk. The mantra was: “I am learning and growing at my own pace. Struggling now does not define my worth or my potential. I celebrate small wins and keep moving forward with effort and kindness toward myself.”
Overall, I would say ChatGPT did a great job in guiding me through my self-reflection. It created a safe and calm environment for me to share my thoughts. Additionally, ChatGPT consistently acknowledged my emotions instead of dismissing it and adjusted its response based on my input. I noticed it remembered key points I mentioned in my earlier responses. For example, I did mention that I hoped to be reassured and understood of my worries. ChatGPT carried that awareness throughout the dialogue, at the start of each response, it would include words of understanding. Such as “carrying all of those feelings at once can feel overwhelming.” or “That must feel really painful watching others talk about how “easy” something was while you were struggling can make the gap feel even wider.”
This consistency made the interaction between me and ChatGPT feel genuine. I was taken aback when ChatGPT asked for evidence for one of my thoughts: “I might just be pursuing the wrong degree.” It said: “If we treat this thought like a hypothesis — something to examine rather than a fact — what evidence do you have for this thought? And what evidence might exist against it, even if it feels small?” This question gave me a ring in my head.
It made me pause for a moment and reflect on whether my belief of “I’m not made for my degree” was based on accumulated frustration or a perception that I had mistaken for fact. It made me reflect on my thoughts more logically rather than letting my emotions consume my thoughts.
Well, this exercise might have helped me discover how AI can be a tool or partner in self-discovery. I also thought that maybe AI could assist therapists by identifying thought patterns and allow psychologists to focus more deeply on treatment planning.

Essay:
In this assignment of “Information to Transformation”, I used prompts from ChatGPT and inserted them into Google Gemini. This is because after chatting with ChatGPT for a while, they will change the model used and want to achieve consistency in the conversation. I mainly used prompt engineering as I want a consistent conversation with the AI. 

I shared about the quarter life crisis I am in currently. I truly feel overwhelmed and stressed everyday with finding a full-time job in a difficult job market and finishing my last semester in school. Finding a full-time job is tough enough, on top of this I still must complete my due diligence as a student (as I should) really gets to me when I have more important things to deal with. I also shared that I broke up early this year and I am not sad about it. The end of the relationship actually shifted more focus into my life, you can think of it as a “wake-up call”; it made me more aware of finding a job and finishing school well. Unfortunately, this increases my stress because this is my future I am dealing with and is literally in my hands.  

Using the Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy (CBT) method in the prompt, Google Gemini asked me what the scariest thought is I have when I think about job search. I said, “what if I do not get a full-time job offer by the time I finish the semester?” It then asked me to give a range from 0-100% of the anxiety I am feeling. I gave it 90%. Following, we listed down evidence for the thought and evidence against. The former, I said “I have not gotten a full-time job offer”. The latter, I said, “I have job interviews going on” and “I am actively applying”. It then came up with an assurance message for me saying that even though everything is very unclear now, I am still actively applying, and interviews are coming up so it does not mean I will fail. It also provided me alternate perspectives to navigate what I am going through like focusing on the process and acknowledging my effort. 

In this exercise, I learnt that I can be quite hard on myself sometimes, just because I have not achieved my end goal I look down on myself slightly. I did not recognize the growth in this whole process and that I have not given up until now. The good thing is that I have the self-awareness in me to know what I am feeling and how I manage it. I shared with Google Gemini whenever I am stressed or need a change of environment, I just hit the gym. This is because the gym is the only place in my life currently where I do not have to deal with job search, I do not have to think of schoolwork, even communicating with people is not a headache, the gym is basically a no-nonsense zone. I also enjoy the endorphins and pain in my muscle when lifting. It is good I have the self-awareness in me to find a place that makes me feel calmer and aligns my thought process. I honestly think I will go crazy if I do not hit the gym. 

Till some extent, doing this exercise makes me think I should give myself credit for making it this far. Instead of resigning and giving up after all the changes that has happened this year, I am still pushing on and trying to achieve greater heights in life. I should celebrate my strength and growth. I have been too focused on trying to get my life together, I did not look back and see how far I have travelled until now. 

Furthermore, this exercise actually gave me an idea of talking to a LLM even though I have friends to listen to me and help me out. This is because sometimes people around us might project their own thoughts and experiences onto you when they give you advice. That may not help because everyone is different, and their experiences is different from yours. However, platforms like ChatGPT or Google Gemini I used, they are built on logic. They are not human and will not speak like people around us. We can even use prompts to structure the conversation we want to have according to our needs. Therefore, the next time my friend does not provide me a helpful advice maybe I can try these platforms for an alternate perspective. I will not throw all my eggs in one basket, believing it will produce all the results I want from it. 

In conclusion, I am actually glad I did this exercise. When Google Gemini asked me what I am facing currently, I answered it seriously describing everything that is going on in my mind. I have never spoke so candidly with heavy emotions in me for awhile now. I have been telling my friends I am stressed and overwhelmed when we talk, but not in a setting where I speak with a heavy heart and so seriously. I usually just hit the gym, play with my cats or close off for a while and not speak to anybody. Chatbot or not, feels good that my efforts were recognized by Google Gemini haha.

Growing up, I was always used to being in a fast academic paced environment: I piled on extracurriculars, took a few too many AP classes, and did as much as I possibly could to prove something to myself, to supply myself with the best opportunities. This continued to my first year of college, where I ended up completing half of my degree by the end of the first year. I was stressed, but I also felt quite accomplished. Following the US’ election results, I also knew I wanted to leave: I’m not a person who dwells on the future I want for myself. When I transferred over, only ~30% of my credits were moved with me. All the classes I took, everything ranging from all my 13 AP classes and 13 college credits, only 6 came with me. In the exemptions I got, my first semester only left me with 3 classes, none of them really STEM centered. I felt unfloored; I feel as though I’m doing less math, less coding, and less in general. I will add however that the shift to a safer environment has allowed me to further dive into things I’m passionate about: hobbies and being informed about the US’ political state (a lot easier to
follow when I’m not being immediately affected). How do I offset the feelings of inadequacy of not doing enough? How do I focus on the good that is to come with a slower paced life?

In creating a prompt to analyze and process my own thoughts, I first wanted to take a more positive approach, which in psychology (as described in the given video) is cognitive
reframing. I prompted ChatGPT 5 (Thinking, Extended Thinking model) to “provide prompts for an LLM to help a user with cognitive reframing”. Like the video, it gave me multiple options for prompts, one long one as an “All in one session prompt”, and other “Targeted mini-prompts”. I then prompted it to “provide me one prompt that incorporates all that is mentioned above, and
encourages the LLM to fully utilize Chain-of-Thought prompting that considers the user's full behavior, background, and context” in order to get one comprehensive prompt that is contextually relevant. I thought it was interesting how instead of fully text based formatting, it gave me code-based replies, sometimes in JSON format as well (due to my prior prompts with
the same model about coding help I’m guessing). Here is the page where I prompted the LLM to provide me with cognitive reframing prompts to use:
https://chatgpt.com/share/690dc6d4-cf68-800a-a6b4-1565d16ea4da


Upon pasting the master prompt and the area in which I wanted further insight in (the entirety of this paper’s first paragraph), GPT gave me areas in which there were thought
distortions detected, and how to counter them. It also gave me different scenarios where I incorporated the given advice, and % chances on success of the advice and results, which
 
allowed me to compartmentalize the effects of these efforts would only be positive. Something that particularly stuck out to me, was the alternative thoughts. “My pace changed; my potential didn't", and “Safety and growth can happen together”. It was the reassurance I was looking for, that my capabilities didn’t diminish in idleness. I now gained insight into how to appreciate the lighter workload and channel it into something different.
It also gave me a practical solution to my feelings of falling behind; on how to self
improve in the areas I specifically felt like I was lacking in. The plan GPT gave me was to begin a flagship project and a math track by myself, working on it 5-8hrs/week to start. When further prompted to “help me devise a 1 month plan for the flagship coding project and math track, based on past knowledge about what classes I have already taken”, it devised a 4 week plan for a coding project and revision of the math concepts I used to do. The plans were incredibly relevant to the subjects I studied before (whether I preferred C++, UI/UX designs, or even the different interdisciplinary math topics I can dive into), mainly because it already retains a history of all the questions I asked pertaining to those subjects, including curating reviews for past exams.
Overall, my experience in this was one of positive outcomes. Having things structured out–like the 4 week plan laid out–gives me a sense of understanding into what I could be doing
instead of feeling stuck. I will genuinely incorporate the advice given to me, one of being kinder to myself and not to doubt my abilities, and the other of how to productively channel my energy into self-improvement! I understand that self-improvement looks different to everybody, but to me I do believe having curiosity for studying and actually partaking in it outside of assignments would make me feel grounded. Question: In our daily lives, we engage in countless conversations with others and with ourselves. Some resemble the transmission or interaction models of communication, while others are transformative—aligned with the transactional model—leading to new perspectives and the co-creation of meaning. Could such an “Ah-Ha” moment also emerge from a conversation with AI? We are living in a rapid prototyping era in which AI has accelerated the development of functional prototypes that allow us to explore the synergy between artificial intelligence and humanity. In this assignment, you will design and use conversational AI to guide a process of self-discovery and reflect critically on the experience.
Essay:
AIH ASSIGNMENT
Assignment brief:
1.	Create and interact with a conversational AI agent of my choice to explore a personal area of awareness.
2.	Write a reflection (max 2 pages)


REFLECTION
Personally, when starting this assignment the area in which I sought greater awareness was the most challenging to come up with, let alone create a conversational Chatbot for. I had to reflect on my personal experiences thoroughly and through this reflection I realised the many limitations that Chatbots are restricted by despite its advancements in recent years. Certain experiences and areas I wished to seek greater awareness in were either far too personal or specific which made it difficult to customise the Chatbot directly to what I was envisioning.

Ultimately, I decided to focus on a conversational Chatbot that would be relevant in the current context of my daily life. Being a fresh undergraduate, navigating the new pace of life that university has to offer me has been exciting yet daunting. I am met with new peers, professors, subjects and even structure. This sudden change was something I struggled and am still struggling to navigate as I find myself feeling overwhelmed and losing my sense of purpose. This was what I focused on when building this Chatbot as I felt that this was something many could relate to, being relevant and common.

The main area I sought greater awareness was to find advice to keep myself grounded in the fast paced environment that is University life. I first went to the web browser of ChatGPT, inputting a prompt with very vague instructions. “Embody the persona of a conversational Chatbot, make it focus on helping students in university like myself find purpose in the fast-paced life of university life.” I was pleasantly surprised to see how much detail each feature held when ChatGPT provided me with a response.
 
1.	It named itself as a Chatbot as a “Casual Persona”, giving itself a name Kai. Instantly producing the goals it intends to achieve as a Chatbot and as a companion.
2.	From the get go, it provided a sample scenario of how it may be utilised by a user. Generating responses based on the degree of distress based on the language used.
Adding on to this step, I decided to take it further in refining certain features to better suit its use as a Chatbot for myself. I looked into making the Chatbot more friendly as well as personal. Given that my Chatbot was one I hoped would cater to fellow university students such as myself, I wanted a Chatbot to feel like a friend that one could consult.

Furthermore, to make this even more holistic, I added another prompt into ChatGPT, “ Make this Chatbot more realistic, adding resources and offer more practical solutions” , adding the additional feature for the Chatbot to prompt the creation of a schedule or plan. ChatGPT was able to very quickly take this prompt and create an entirely new persona – Jamie who could also add additional insights for the user to ponder about while being counselled.

Through personal use of this temporary Chatbot I used, I found that to navigate this hectic period of a new chapter in my life, I should find small meaningful ways to be grounded while motivating myself with a schedule and ‘ToDos’. Though tips that are fairly simple, these pieces of advice were given in a comforting and casual tone which made it a lot easier to internalize and served as a reminder for myself.

When viewing holistically, I enjoyed this assignment thoroughly. It was interesting to see how ChatGPT, the mode of AI I chose for this assignment, so quickly adapted to the prompts I gave it and changed to fit what I was specifically looking for in a conversational chatbot. It amazed me to witness how quickly I could ‘build’ a simple working Chatbot even with the trials we had within class. I hope to continue exploring these features and delve more into different types of Chatbots, especially with the use of other AI models.

Question: In our daily lives, we engage in countless conversations with others and with ourselves. Some resemble the transmission or interaction models of communication, while others are transformative—aligned with the transactional model—leading to new perspectives and the co-creation of meaning. Could such an “Ah-Ha” moment also emerge from a conversation with AI? We are living in a rapid prototyping era in which AI has accelerated the development of functional prototypes that allow us to explore the synergy between artificial intelligence and humanity. In this assignment, you will design and use conversational AI to guide a process of self-discovery and reflect critically on the experience.
Essay:
For this assignment, I chose to reflect on a conflict with a close friend during a friendly futsal session that happened quite a few years back, however, it is an incident that has been etched in my mind for a period of time. This incident was where I exploded and was the first time I felt so angry. As football has been a huge part of my life since I was a child, I will try my best to make time for it weekly and it was a good way to unwind from my academic stress. During the futsal match, my close friend unexpectedly slid in with a hard tackle, causing a sharp pain in my shin. In that moment, anger got the better of me and I impulsively shoved him and shouted “it’s only a friendly match, what is your issue?” He tried to calm me down and explained his reasoning for doing that, however, I was not in the mood to hear any explanations as I felt that it was extremely unnecessary and that it was supposed to be just a friendly game. The anger I was feeling stayed with me for a few days, and I did not reply to his messages when he tried to contact me after that incident. As he was my close friend, I felt that I should have been more understanding and listen to his side of the story before letting anger get the better of me. In that moment, I realized that my strong reaction was not just about the pain that I felt in the moment, but it also touched on sportsmanship, and how I would handle my emotional triggers with people that I deeply care about.
To truly understand why anger got the better of me, I decided to use Perplexity as I had the pro version that was provided from the school. I crafted an informal, friendly Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) prompt, and requesting that the AI kept the conversation casual, conversational, and to act as a supportive friend. Throughout the conversation, the AI invited me to talk through what had happened, unpack my thoughts and feelings. Feeling super frustrated about the experience, I used my laptop in the comfort of my home and begin typing away into Perplexity. The AI started the conversation with asking questions on how I felt emotionally about the situation, and prompted me to consider not just my anger, but other emotions such as embarrassment, which I had not consciously acknowledged. The casual and friendly tone allowed to lower my guard and speak honestly, without worrying about any judgmental opinion that the AI might provide.
In my interaction with Perplexity, I tried experimenting with different AI prompt strategies to improve the quality of my self-reflection. I decided to use a chain-of-thought prompting style, which encouraged the AI to guide me step by step from describing the incident, understanding my emotional reactions, to further reflections and ways that I can possibly resolve the tenstion between my close friend and I. This logical process kept the conversation structured and thorough.
I added modifiers to my prompt such as “act as a supportive friend”, “keep the conversation simple and easy to understand”, “break down my thoughts and help me understand them better”. This modifiers helped set a tone that was empathetic and felt like a safe space to converse.
To further enrich my reflection, I tried using a multi-perspective approach, whereby the AI switched between gentle CBT questioning and where it acted as an observer, it asked me to view the situation objectively (for example, “If you saw two friends in a similar situation, what would you have done to help the friend that was injured?” “How can you be more
 
sensitive to their emotions?”. These new perspectives helped me gained a better understanding and allowed me to take a step back from my own emotions, helping me view conflicts more objectively.
Another aspect of the AI-guided process was how it supported the reconstruction of my social reality around the incident. I saw myself as a victim of unfair and aggressive play, and my close friend was thoughtless and decided to just tackle me in a rough manner. The AI prompted me to revisit assumptions about intent (for example, “Did my friend tackle to harm, or was it just a competitive reflex?”). As I reflected, I realized how common it was in sports for emotions to get the better of anybody and for actions to be misinterpreted, which challenged my judgment that my friend had deliberately crossed a line. Through this process, social realities such as unspoken sporting codes among friends are co-constructed and open to re-negotiation. The AI’s ability to provide alternative scenarios and perspective shifting allowed me to change the way I view the tackle, but put me into a different perspective to consider forgiveness, and communication with my close friend. This perspective enabled me to reconstruct my understanding of the event as a shared human moment, rather than one- sided affair.
Looking back, and through the various conversations that I had with the AI, I recognized that my friend is just naturally competitive. Although I had seen him make similar tackles before, it had never happened to me because we were always on the same team and this time around, we were placed in different teams. Through the conversation, I recalled that I was feeling extremely overwhelmed by the different issues that I was facing in school and some other personal issues with my family, these issues may have contributed to the way that I have reacted towards my friend as well. I also learned that my anger was not focused around the tackle, but the feeling of being disrespected by someone that was close to me. The AI shifted my perspective, and helped me view that my friend was apologetic after the incident, even if he did not express it verbally. Through this process, I realized that ignoring him may only worsened the relationship and bond that we once shared, and that a simple conversation, even if awkward, will help to restore trust and the close bond that we once shared.
Overall, I was surprised by how much insight and expertise I gained just by conversing with AI. The AI offered a safe space to break down my thoughts and emotions logically, without the judgment of a real person. I also learned various techniques from the AI, such as taking a moment to calm down and eventually asked my friend why he did the tackle on me and try to understand his side of the story before making baseless conclusions. Lastly, with the appropriate prompts, even AI can turn this event into a meaningful transformation from just information and emotions.

Question: In our daily lives, we engage in countless conversations with others and with ourselves. Some resemble the transmission or interaction models of communication, while others are transformative—aligned with the transactional model—leading to new perspectives and the co-creation of meaning. Could such an “Ah-Ha” moment also emerge from a conversation with AI? We are living in a rapid prototyping era in which AI has accelerated the development of functional prototypes that allow us to explore the synergy between artificial intelligence and humanity. In this assignment, you will design and use conversational AI to guide a process of self-discovery and reflect critically on the experience.
Essay:
Assignment - Information to Transformation
I have always wanted to eat more healthily but I did not know where to start. So, I thought of planning my meals with proper nutrition, but I didn’t want to waste time to research and consolidate it by myself.
Therefore, I used chatgpt to create an LLM prompt to ask the user to give more information about themselves for nutrition requirements and meal planning. I wanted the questions to be as specific and relevant as possible with a good logic flow. I also wanted the agent to keep the conversation friendly, encouraging and clear so I integrated LLM, chain of thought, and prompt engineering to create the master prompt below. To make it more user friendly, I tried to break the questions up to smaller parts so that the user does not feel overwhelmed when answering the questions. To reduce confusion, I also prompt the
agent to give some examples after asking the questions (What is your nutrition goal? e.g. lose weight, build muscle, eat healthier etc).


 
I also requested to have all the information summarized at the end and create a personalised meal plan that meets their goals, preferences and lifestyle while including macro tracking of calories, proteins, carbs and fats for nutrition requirements. I noticed how the agent took into consideration my dietary habits like not eating chocolate and nuts as well as digestion problems. I also
realised that the agent used emojis and positive expressions like “Great,
Awesome, Perfect, Got it!” to make the conversations more human like and
friendly. Afterwards, it created a 7-day personalised meal plan based on my responses and needs. I find it really interesting and surprising as it gave me different food for each day so that my meals will not be that boring.


It also gave me a summarised macro
tracking of the nutrients for the week with suggestions to focus on soft and steamed vegetables for my digestion
issue. Something I noticed was that the protein meat was the same either
chicken or fish or toufu so I prompted chatgpt to switch some meats to pork and duck. It immediately changed the meal plan according to my request and I find it very amusing and fun to switch the menu up for different days. It also reminded me to go for lean tenderloin or loin slices to reduce fat and improve digestion which I find it very meticulous and caring.
Overall, it was easy and pleasant to converse with the agent. I learnt to apply the topics I have learnt in class and develop useful generative AI solutions with chatgpt. At first, I thought this assignment will be difficult to do but after trying out and changing the prompts, I realised that it was quite simple and fun to
do. Usually, I only used chatgpt for summarizing topics and idea generations. But because of this activity, I found out that I could prompt chatgpt to develop an LLM which gave me a very cool and new experience. After this activity, I will try to achieve my personal goal of eating more healthily by having a balanced diet with fruits, vegetables, chicken and fish in my meals. I am now more interested and eager to learn about
AI, delve deeper into LLMs, and explore the potential impacts AI could have on our future.

Essay:
Personal Area
I decided to consult with ChatGPT on methods to dealing with burnout. Perhaps it could be the sudden transition from polytechnic’s life to university’s life. Perhaps it could be the constant worrying on future matters such as employment and loan repayment.
These have generally led me to feeling demotivated in studying and performing well. Having a clear awareness that I am not performing at my optimum ability lately make me feel worse about myself.
Integration of Different Topics
Prompt Engineering – Context
I designed my prompt to include context on how I have been feeling and guilty pleasures like procrastinating, sleeping late, and skipping meals. I then followed it by two
questions on the “diagnosis” and “treatment” or Cognitive-Behavioural Therapy (CBT) approach to combat it.
Chain-of-Thought
ChatGPT response on both the “diagnosis” and “treatment” respectively have been broken down and evaluated separately.
For the “diagnosis”, it has explained and elaborated on each of my symptoms with
possible reasons why I am feeling this way. It soon ended with a conclusion which align with my belief that it is an academic burnout.
While for the “treatment”, upon request, it showed a CBT approach with 5 steps. Mainly identifying unhelpful thoughts, challenging and reframing them, behavioural activation, emotional regulation techniques, and self-compassion training. It even provided a
reflection template to validate and regulate with my own emotions which may be handy during stressful situations.
Reconstruction of Social Realities
Along the way, I have asked a lot of questions which carries my firm belief. For example, ChatGPT has shown unhelpful thoughts as negative thoughts like “Others are doing better than me”. This has widely contrasted with my belief that negative thoughts are sometimes helpful by boosting stress and thus task completion. Personally, I find it effective as that is what I have been doing since my Secondary and Polytechnic years. If I do not sense the urgency like I am behind others, I would not have pushed myself to pay attention during class and revise for tests. The outcome is rather desirable
considering it has land me into SMU so why are negative thoughts discouraged? I am positive that this is a common practice exercised by my peers in associating negative thoughts with good outcomes. Always chanting the statement “I am going to fail” after finishing a test and excelling afterwards for some.
 
However, ChatGPT has challenged my belief by explaining that these negative thoughts may be helpful at first, but they are not sustainable in the long run. It even referenced
back to my symptoms on the detrimental effects negative thoughts cause, commencing the stress-procrastination-guilt loop and increasing a stress hormone which has
precisely affected my lifestyle habits. It feels like negative thoughts always lead to good outcomes because I act on them. This has led to my brain associating negativity with productivity, only if I criticise myself then I get moving. Frequent criticism has led to my current state and low self-esteem. True that negative thoughts are no longer helpful, I guess. Instead of relying on toxicity, I should focus on the benefits and goals.
Design of Conversational Agent
Rather than using ChatGPT’s generated responses in a static manner, I probe and inquire on their minor details to obtain a better understanding. By leveraging on the previously provided context, it has also produced more relevant and personalised content which led to countless “A-ha!” moments. Even for the additional questions.
Insight and Life Influence
One insight that I have gained from this experience is the process of reframing by asking if it is really the case or 100% true. Previously, I had the tendency to drown myself in
negativity and assume that people like me only for being smart thus there is no room for failure.
Through reframing and reflecting on facts like real-life experiences, I realised that my friends stood with me thick and thin during challenging times. Moreover, my family members have never berated me when I failed to do well. Instead, they have offered their continuous support and encouragement. Frankly, this have made me feel better and start to cherish the people around me. In facing similar negative thoughts in the future, I may attempt to adopt this practice.
Overall Reflection
During my burnout phase, I continuously asked and criticised myself on my current state. “Previously you were okay, why now like this?” “No wonder, you are part of the strawberry generation.” “Stop over pitying yourself, everyone is facing the same thing.” I am genuinely glad that I decided to touch on this topic for this assignment as ChatGPT has resonated with my thoughts well and encouraged me to be gentle towards myself.
When I was reading through the unhelpful thoughts portion, I suddenly realised how harsh and mean I have been treating myself. It almost felt like ChatGPT knew what I was thinking, each example of unhelpful thoughts matched my daily thoughts list. Upon
showing the damaging effects of each example, it instantly hit me on why I always lack confidence, have low self-worth, and feel dispirited.
I understand now, how did my burnout come about and how I can tackle it.

Question: In our daily lives, we engage in countless conversations with others and with ourselves. Some resemble the transmission or interaction models of communication, while others are transformative—aligned with the transactional model—leading to new perspectives and the co-creation of meaning. Could such an “Ah-Ha” moment also emerge from a conversation with AI? We are living in a rapid prototyping era in which AI has accelerated the development of functional prototypes that allow us to explore the synergy between artificial intelligence and humanity. In this assignment, you will design and use conversational AI to guide a process of self-discovery and reflect critically on the experience.
Essay:
For this exercise, I chose to explore stress management and overcommitment in my personal and academic life. As midterms approached, I found myself feeling overwhelmed while juggling an internship, job applications, academic projects, tests, and other commitments. This often left me fatigued, emotionally drained, and stressed. To better understand the root causes of my stress, my decision-making patterns, and ways to achieve a healthier balance, I decided to engage with ChatGPT as a conversational AI agent, simulating a reflective dialogue similar to coaching.
I began by asking the AI to provide prompts for guiding a Singaporean university student through a reflective exploration of stress, overcommitment, and work-life balance during a busy academic period. It suggested several phases, including identifying stress and overcommitment, understanding causes and patterns, reflecting on coping and self-care, and planning for growth and balance. The AI provided relatable questions such as, “Do you find it difficult to rest or take a break, especially when you see your peers constantly working hard?” and “How do you feel about the culture of busyness in Singapore universities — do you think it affects your sense of balance?” I then asked it to generate a single, ready-to-use prompt, which became:
“Act as a supportive AI mentor for a Singaporean university student reflecting on stress, overcommitment, and work-life balance during a busy academic period. Ask gentle, open-ended questions to help them explore their stress sources, coping habits, and ways to find balance. Keep the tone empathetic and relatable. Start with: ‘How have you been feeling lately with all your schoolwork and commitments?’”
When I shared that I felt overwhelmed managing schoolwork, internships, and job applications, the AI asked about my schedule, which parts of the day were most stressful, and how my mind and body responded. I explained that switching from internship tasks during the day to academics and job applications in the evening left me physically and emotionally drained, causing fatigue and anxiety.
The AI summarized my responses and offered practical strategies. These included prioritizing and chunking tasks into “must-do today,” “important but flexible,” and “can wait”; scheduling mini-breaks of 5 to 10 minutes to reset; batching similar tasks to reduce mental switching; setting boundaries to avoid work outside certain hours; conducting
self-compassion check-ins; and connecting with friends, mentors, or counselors for support. It also suggested a simple daily plan: morning exercise and reviewing top school tasks, daytime internship work with a short lunch break, evening focus on schoolwork and job applications, mini wind-downs, and a 10:30 pm bedtime for at least seven hours of sleep.
The AI encouraged me to notice the lighter parts of the day and adjust based on energy levels, recognizing that even small wins contribute to balance.
I concluded by thanking the AI and deciding to implement its suggestions. This exercise helped me recognize patterns behind my overcommitment, explore healthier coping mechanisms, and gain practical strategies to manage stress.
Through interacting with the AI, I became more aware of the patterns underlying my overcommitment. I realized that much of my stress stems not only from a heavy workload but also from internalized pressures to be constantly productive and to meet external

expectations, such as peers’ performance or societal standards. The AI helped me see that my sense of self-worth had been closely tied to productivity, and that this mindset contributed to fatigue, anxiety, and occasional feelings of being stuck. I also gained insight into practical ways to manage this, such as structuring my day into focused blocks, taking micro-breaks, setting boundaries, and practicing self-compassion. These strategies made me realize that achieving balance is not about completing everything perfectly, but about prioritizing, pacing myself, and making deliberate choices aligned with my well-being.
Recognizing this gives me a more intentional approach to managing stress and approaching future busy periods more sustainably.
The process of engaging with a conversational AI was surprisingly insightful and personally validating. Unlike traditional advice or self-reflection alone, the AI provided a structured,
non-judgmental dialogue that guided me through identifying stressors, reflecting on patterns, and generating actionable strategies. I appreciated how prompt design and chain-of-thought interactions allowed the conversation to evolve naturally, making the AI feel like a counselor rather than just a tool. This experience highlighted the potential of AI for reflective practice and self-awareness, especially when navigating complex personal and academic challenges. Overall, the assignment reinforced the value of deliberate reflection, helped me articulate my stress patterns more clearly, and equipped me with practical strategies that I can apply in daily life to achieve a healthier balance.
Beyond the immediate strategies for managing stress, this exercise also highlighted broader lessons about self-awareness and learning. By carefully crafting prompts and engaging in chain-of-thought dialogue with the AI, I recognized how reflection can be structured and intentional, rather than passive. The conversation encouraged me to reconstruct my perspective on productivity and achievement within the context of Singapore’s academic culture, helping me see that rest and balance are not signs of weakness but essential for sustained performance. It also demonstrated the potential of AI as a reflective tool, simulating multi-agent reasoning by balancing rational planning with emotional insight.
Moving forward, I see opportunities to use AI-guided reflection not only for stress management but also for career planning, personal development, and goal-setting, giving me a practical and accessible way to pause, evaluate, and make deliberate choices. Overall, this experience reinforced the importance of self-compassion, intentional planning, and reflective practice, providing both immediate strategies and long-term skills to navigate challenging periods more mindfully and sustainably.

Some resemble the transmission or interaction models of communication, while others are transformative—aligned with the transactional model—leading to new perspectives and the co-creation of meaning. Could such an “Ah-Ha” moment also emerge from a conversation with AI? We are living in a rapid prototyping era in which AI has accelerated the development of functional prototypes that allow us to explore the synergy between artificial intelligence and humanity. Essay:
The personal area of awareness I chose to explore is the “Role Conflict” faced by many
student-athletes, including myself. The “Role Conflict” refers to the tension between personal identity outside of sports, and the public image along with people’s expectation of a “machine” athlete.

Being in the national team for canoeing means my daily life is scheduled around training and competition, leaving little to no time for anything else. While this fosters discipline, it has led to a kind of reconstruction of social reality where my public image has suffocated my personal identity. The biggest source of anxiety is that I feel like an imposter when I step outside of the sports world. My success on the water does not validate my worth as a student or a person. I am terrified of letting go of this “athlete” life because I am unsure of who my true self is anymore. I believe that through this exercise I will be able to develop intrapersonal intelligence as a conversation with an AI agent could help me to discover new perspectives that myself or others were not able to.

The AI Agent I chose was Gemini Advanced (Google Conversational Agent). The selection was strategic for a few reasons. The first was its familiarity and efficiency. I’ve consistently used Gemini for academic research and as a tool to answer my own general curiosity. Gemini is designed to use data from past conversations to deliver more helpful and personalised responses in the future. Starting the self-discovery process on a platform I already trust and frequently interact with ensured I could focus purely on the prompt engineering and reflection, rather than learning a new user interface.
Additionally, its advanced reasoning capabilities powered by its underlying models, excels at maintaining a complex, sustained chain-of-thought over multiple turns, which was crucial for the planned dialogue.

I first started by giving a prompt to Gemini, giving it the necessary context and strategy required for our conversation. The goal was to force the agent into a non-linear, coaching-style dialogue to avoid simple information delivery. Hence I ask it to adopt a socratic teaching style to allow more critical thinking.

Following this, I explored different areas, such as whether I lack necessary skillsets and knowledge, or how I believed that the muscles I have built over the years would all be wasted once I am retired as an athlete, etc.

The new awareness came when I reflected on how I also viewed my life out of sports as a competition, leading to burnouts.


Through deeper conversations with Gemini, I realise that my failure to thrive is not a lack of time, but a lack of periodisation in my personal life. Gemini suggested the need to intentionally create three distinct life seasons to prevent such burnouts.


This framework provides an immediate path to developing my intrapersonal intelligence by giving me a clear, structured language to understand and manage my stress. It provided me with an actionable tool. When I feel overwhelmed, I can stop and ask: "Am I trying to do 'Off-Season' deep development work during my 'Competition Season' peak week?" By scheduling my rest as a method to increase my “Return on Energy”, it reduces the guilt of needing rest and defines a clear, protected space for the deep, meaningful work I may want to do.The "Ah-Ha" is realizing that sustainability comes from structured rest and varying intensity, not just relentless effort.

The assignment successfully facilitated a movement from information, i.e. I have a time management problem, to transformation, where I now know how to manage my personal identity. The conversational agent design was key. By implementing a virtual multi-agent LLM system within a single agent's prompt, I forced the output to be multifaceted and challenging. The chain-of-thought strategy prevented the AI from simply listing facts and ensured the agent provided the required "friction" necessary for a genuine transactional communication model. The conversation felt less like talking to a search engine and more like a focused, internal dialogue externalised and given structure by the AI.

This exercise has truly allowed me to explore the synergy achieved between the AI's objective process and my subjective experience. My original thoughts on the AI's utility were primarily transactional. I viewed Gemini as a sophisticated tool for academic research and information retrieval; essentially, a smart search engine. I expected it to simply list a couple of options or set a table for me.

The main takeaway, however, is that for deep self-discovery, the AI's true value is not in its intelligence, but its unemotional objectivity. It acted as a neutral, yet highly skilled, agent that could point out psychological patterns in my life that my own emotions and personal experiences prevented me from seeing. It became an externalised, structured internal dialogue.

This led to the most critical realisation where it pointed out that my greatest athletic strength, the structured management of intensity and discipline, was also my greatest personal weakness outside of sport. Because the AI didn't care about my personal feelings but only my system's efficiency, it could confidently tell me I was ‘overtraining’ my life. This allowed me to accept and define my dual identity.

I remember my original thought clearly: I used to see my personal downtime as a leak in my performance system, a flaw of who I was supposed to be. For example, when I would try to spend two uninterrupted hours learning out of syllabus, I would internally calculate the number of training minutes I was “missing”, feeling immense anxiety. Now, thanks to the periodisation framework, I have changed my perspective. I view the same two hours of learning as essential psychological strength training, it is a pre-scheduled, non-negotiable "Off-Season" allocation for myself. The conversation felt less like talking to a search engine and more like a focused, internal dialogue externalised and given structure by the AI. This ultimately allowed me to accept and define my dual identity, turning my perceived weakness into my greatest sustainable strength.

Each prompt led naturally to another, often steering me with gentle “why?” and “how?” until I dug into the root my issue which in this context is self-doubt in leadership positions. This made the conversation feel meaningful and safe enough to probe my personal leadership challenges. In fact, experts note that ChatGPT can prompt users with CBT-style questions to identify thought patterns (Chloemiller, 2025), which matched my experience.
I quickly realised that getting useful advice from ChatGPT depended heavily on how I framed my prompts. Something that helped me increase my
proficiency with ChatGPT was an insight from OpenAI’s president, where he shared about a four- step prompt formula, which starts by stating the users goal, format, constraints, and end of with context (Matthews, 2025). What I would usually put into my prompts is that I would start the chat by clearly describing my role and what kind of help I wanted. Then I added specifics like preferred output style (lists, examples, reflective questions) and any guardrails. This level of detail has paid off for multiple of my taskings and this is even backed by experts where they point out that the more context you give, the better the output (Stillman, 2025), and clear constraints help reduce hallucinations. From this habit, when I asked ChatGPT to generate a LLM prompt for me it naturally added the line to avoid generic advice and focus on my personal scenarios. The result was a conversation that
stayed on track and felt customized to my needs

I chose ChatGPT for this exercise because it offered the right mix of flexibility and reliability as other tools have their niches. From my experience, Perplexity AI is great at scouring the web for academic answers or even video transcripts, but it felt less suited to a reflective and structured dialogue. DeepSeek and Grok are powerful in their own way, and I use them mainly for mathematical breakdowns or economic teachings, so ChatGPT’s conversational skill made it the natural choice.
This exercise also resonated deeply with my personality as an INTJ. INTJs naturally emphasise logic and objective information over subjective emotions (MSEd, 2024b), and we tend to organise thoughts in a structured and cause-effect way. ChatGPT played right into that style as whenever I felt distracted by feelings or uncertainty, I would articulate them and the ChatGPT would translate them into a clear question or logical outline. In effect, I was using the AI as an external “thinking partner” to sort through my ideas methodically, which felt tailor-made for my style.

In the end, this experiment with ChatGPT was like a mirror reflecting how I think. When I gave it well-designed prompts and enough context, it gave me back relevant and grounded insights that cut
deep. The process reinforced a simple truth and that is AI’s value lies not in mind-reading but in helping us articulate what we already know in a new way. This assignment helped me came away with a sharper vision of my leadership goals and a checklist of practical action points (figure 2). The whole journey reaffirmed a simple truth which I have been sharing to many of my friends which is that even advanced AI needs clear human guidance to be effective.

Question: In our daily lives, we engage in countless conversations with others and with ourselves. Some resemble the transmission or interaction models of communication, while others are transformative—aligned with the transactional model—leading to new perspectives and the co-creation of meaning. Could such an “Ah-Ha” moment also emerge from a conversation with AI? We are living in a rapid prototyping era in which AI has accelerated the development of functional prototypes that allow us to explore the synergy between artificial intelligence and humanity. In this assignment, you will design and use conversational AI to guide a process of self-discovery and reflect critically on the experience.
Essay:
For me, I was hoping to be able to reframe my thoughts with regards to how I approach pressure situations. This has always been something that has plagued me since I was young; that in high pressure situations, specifically sporting competitions, I have a tendency to underperform and that is something I hoped to be able to reframe my thinking to be able to cope with the pressure and in turn, have better performances.
When designing the prompt, I was reminded of the CO-STAR framework and tried to get the LLM to design a prompt that fulfilled the different aspects of CO-STAR. The initial prompt I designed was “Provide a prompt for an LLM to bring a user who has performance anxiety to reframe their thoughts and change their mentality. This prompt should ask the LLM to
respond in the style of a support coach.” This incorporated some aspects of CO-STAR
such as context where I explained that the user “has performance anxiety” and the
objective is to “reframe their thoughts and change their mentality.” I also requested the LLM to “respond in the style of a support coach”, which would hopefully return a result that is more encouraging and supportive. Furthermore, I used perplexity as my choice of LLM as it houses multiple different LLMs and picks the most applicable one to use based on the user's query. With all of that, the LLM returned the following prompt which I then proceeded to use and let the LLM guide me through the experience.

When I shared my struggle with the LLM, the first heading it returned to me was as follows

To me, this was a little strange. Usually, when counsellors or people in general try to validate your feelings, they do not necessarily say it outright. By doing so, it feels forced and unnatural, like they are validating your feelings for the sake of it, not because they actually care. I guess this could be due to the prompt where validation of feelings was listed as one of the jobs of the LLM and so it was returning what was prompted to it.

Nonetheless, the following segments were indeed quite helpful to my situation. I liked the part where I was asked to challenge my negative thoughts. I think a lot of pressure and nerves I faced stemmed from my all-or-nothing thinking as the LLM pointed out, where I see wins and losses as binary. If I win, that means I am good and if I lose, it means that I am bad. However, the LLM prompted me to look beyond that. It prompted me to think about how wins and losses were not entirely a measure of my ability and to think of them as learning experiences. Ultimately, the score is just a number and the important thing is the learning and the fun derived from playing the sport. I think this was especially helpful to me as many of my bad mindset stems from this issue of not being able to perform well in competitions. One example of this is that I tend to give up after falling behind in a match. I told this to the LLM, and it reminded me that thoughts were not facts and that “your skills
don’t disappear just because you are trailing.” To me, that has always been a big challenge. Whenever I fall behind in a game, I am always thinking of the next one already and I lose focus on the current game. However, the game is never over until I’ve lost. Just because I am trailing, does not necessarily mean that the game is already lost, and it certainly does not have an impact on my skill.
This showed me the power your mind and your thoughts have over you. When I was reflecting on these negative thoughts that I had, I realised that what I thought translated to how I played. If I had thought that I was going to lose, I played as if I had already lost: passive, rushed and certainly not how I would have played in training. Yet my skills have not changed at all, but I am playing as though they did. Through this exercise, I am more aware of the importance of my thoughts and how reframing them can be a powerful tool to improve my game without actually. The LLM also provided useful information on how I can reframe these thoughts such as viewing every point as a new game. It also provided practical tips such as visualisation and breathing exercises.
Overall, this exercise was helpful in helping me to reflect on a long-term problem that I have been facing. An advantage of turning to an LLM for help was that there was no fear of judgement or scrutiny. Usually, that is what holds me back from seeking help. However, with an LLM, it does not have actual feelings and so I was able to express myself more freely. However, this lack of feelings also serves as a double-edged sword as I could definitely feel the difference in empathy between the AI and a real person. I did not get the same feeling of being understood by the AI as I would have with a regular person.
Nonetheless, it was a good experience to be able to slow down and reflect based on the guide by the AI; and the prompts were definitely helpful in helping me start to reframe my thoughts.

Essay:
Information to Transformation: Using Conversational AI for Career Self-Discovery

Context – Anxiety in a Competitive Job Market

As a final-year Computer Science student preparing to graduate, I was overwhelmed by anxiety about entering the job market. News about hiring freezes, competitive entry tests, and challenging technical interviews made me feel unprepared and incompetent. Each time I thought about upcoming assessments, my confidence dropped further. I realized that this anxiety stemmed not from the lack of effort but from the absence of a structured approach to preparation. Hence, I decided to turn to conversational AI to guide me through this
self-discovery process to find clarity, regain control, and create a concrete plan forward.

Designing My Conversational AI Agents

I used ChatGPT as my primary platform because of its accessibility and flexibility for prototyping. Initially, I started a single conversation where I simply asked questions about how to prepare for technical interviews, portfolio building, and job-search strategy. However, as I interacted with the AI, I realized I could apply the concept of “AI for AI” where I used AI to help me design a better AI assistant. I first used one chat to explore prompts, frameworks, and strategies, and from there, I created two specialized versions of the agent:
●Career Coach AI: This chat guided me in developing clarity on my goals, resume positioning, and application strategy.

●Technical Coach AI: This second chat focused on interview preparation — data structures, algorithms, and mock questions.
Through this iterative design, I was essentially engaging in the Era of Prototyping, where ideas can be quickly tested and refined using generative AI. The process reflected an agile mindset: prototype, test, iterate which allowed me to create personalized agents that suited my emotional and technical needs.
The AI’s responses were often questioning and adaptive. Sometimes, it would ask whether it could perform certain new tasks, such as tracking progress or generating mock schedules, showing an almost self-reflective quality. This interactivity made the experience more dynamic than static search. It felt like a living feedback loop between human and machine cognition.

Integration of Key AI and Communication Concepts

Throughout this process, I noticed that my self-discovery was not just personal but also a cognitive reconstruction. I was, in a sense, reconstructing my own social and mental reality through dialogue with AI. Initially, I used simple prompts to gather information, but over time, I refined them into well-engineered prompts that elicited deeper, more reflective responses. This refinement mirrored chain-of-thought reasoning, where each AI response built upon previous reflections, helping me articulate hidden assumptions and emotions.
By creating two separate yet complementary conversations one with a Career Coach AI and another with a Technical Coach AI, I was essentially implementing a multi-agent LLM setup, where different agents handled distinct cognitive domains but worked toward a shared goal:

reducing anxiety and building clarity. In this way, the project became not only a personal reflection but also an experiment in how AI design principles can enhance human introspection and emotional growth.

The “Ah-Ha” Moment

My “Ah-Ha” moment came when I realized that the job search process is not a singular goal but a series of smaller, manageable systems that can be supported by multiple tools including AI. I had initially seen the job hunt as a personal struggle driven by self-doubt, but through my AI conversations, my mindset shifted from “I am not ready” to “I can prepare strategically.”
In one conversation, the AI mapped out a possible weekly plan for balancing coursework, LeetCode practice, and application reviews. Seeing a concrete structure turned abstract anxiety into actionable control. I also discovered that ChatGPT could help me design specialized agentic AIs which are mini “agents” that automate parts of my preparation, such as tracking progress or summarizing company profiles. This expanded my perception of AI beyond a mere Q&A tool to an active collaborator in my personal development journey.

Reflections and Learnings

This experience taught me several lessons about both myself and AI-human collaboration. I realized that my anxiety was amplified by uncertainty and lack of structure. Once I visualized a plan and externalized my thoughts into a conversation, clarity naturally followed. I learned that self-discovery can emerge not only from introspection but also through dialogue even with an AI.
I also recognized AI’s limitations. At times, ChatGPT’s responses felt generic or repetitive, especially when I expressed emotional fatigue rather than factual queries. However, this pushed me to refine my prompts to be specific, contextual, and instructive. In doing so, I discovered that effective prompting mirrors effective thinking: clarity in communication leads to clarity in thought.
Through this process, AI functioned primarily as a tool, but one that mirrored my own reasoning back to me. It helped me externalize scattered thoughts into structured plans: a digital cognitive mirror. More broadly, it revealed how AI could serve as a co-pilot for human growth, blending rational analysis with emotional reflection.
Moving forward, I intend to use conversational AI regularly for career planning, journaling, and structured decision-making.
